revision_note: Phase A.1 (Retrieval Profile Separation): the web-side AI collaborator reviewed Phase A's original flat schema and correctly identified that it conflated four independent axes. Restructured into embedding_space / encoder_execution / score_calibration / fusion_profile so each can version independently -- e.g. the MCP keeps embedding_space=dsrs-v1 unchanged while deliberately using a NEW fusion_profile (RRF) instead of reproducing the browser's current one. Also corrected two claims from the original version (see each section's own note) and fixed a document-count inconsistency (2675 vs 2676 -- see score_calibration.caveat). Second review round added a fifth layer, index_profile (I), after correctly flagging that this file's own migration_note still listed 'chunking policy' as an embedding_space-version trigger -- chunking changes WHAT gets projected into the space (which text spans become vectors, how per-chunk hits fold back into a per-document score), not the coordinate system itself. DSRS is now E + Q + I + C + F.
purpose: Canonical, verified identity of the retrieval behavior that produces today's DSRS results. Split into five independently-versionable layers per DSRS = E + Q + I + C + F: Embedding Space, Encoder Execution, Index/Corpus Projection, Score Calibration, Fusion Policy. A server-side MCP retriever must reproduce E to make cosine against existing corpus vectors valid at all; it may deliberately use a different Q, I, C, or F, as long as that's an explicit, named choice, not a silent drift.

embedding_space.query_prefix: 为这个句子生成表示以用于检索相关文章：
embedding_space.note: This is the layer that actually determines whether cosine similarity against existing corpus vectors is meaningful at all. Different model / tokenizer / pooling / instruction = genuinely different coordinate system (E_A(x) ~ E_B(x) does not hold) = cosine is meaningless. This is the layer a server-side encoder MUST match exactly.
embedding_space.known_limitation_tokenizer_unk_collapse_: Measured via Phase C1.1 (scripts/phase-c-encoder-compare/c1_1_tokenizer_audit.mjs), triggered by a real finding in the C0 oracle: the queries "DSRS", "AICL", "CASP", "SSSP", "MCP", and "∀x∃y" all produced byte-identical 512-dim vectors (confirmed via SHA-256). Root cause, confirmed by direct tokenization for THIS specific query class (short, entirely-out-of-vocabulary Latin acronyms / symbol strings, ~4 characters, tested 6 instances): the ENTIRE query content after the instruction prefix collapsed to a single shared [UNK] token, so the input_ids sequence (and therefore the embedding) became identical across all 6, regardless of what the original text was. Confirmed this is span-level, not per-character, on this evidence: "AI 主體性" (OOV "AI" + real Chinese tail) does NOT collide, because the non-OOV tail still differentiates the sequence. Scope discipline: this is confirmed for pure-OOV short acronym/symbol queries specifically -- do NOT extrapolate to a general claim that this tokenizer never falls back to subword splitting for any/all out-of-vocabulary Latin spans (e.g. longer strings, different character composition were not tested). Practical implication for the tested class: semantic-channel similarity is NOT reliable for a query that is entirely a short, uncommon Latin acronym or symbol string with this model -- exact/lexical/dictionary matching must carry that specific query class, not semantic alone. Real property of BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5's tokenizer for the tested cases, not a bug in this pipeline; relevant to Phase D's fusion design.

encoder_execution.model_revision: browser still unpinned -- production `pipeline()` call has no `revision` option, so it tracks Xenova/bge-small-zh-v1.5's `main`. Status: 'reproduction-verified for commit 75c43b069aac4d136ba6bc1122f995fedcfd2781' as of 2026-08-15, closed in two steps. Phase C1.3 first pinned this revision in a Node q8 run and got the same cosine RANGE against the browser oracle as the unpinned run -- suggestive but, as the second review round correctly pointed out, matching an aggregate statistic against a third reference (the browser oracle) is not a direct proof that unpinned-node output equals pinned-node output. Phase C1.3.1 closed that gap directly: ran unpinned (`main`) and pinned (`75c43b0...`) node-q8 in the SAME process against all 30 oracle queries and compared via SHA-256 -- 30/30 byte-identical. So `Q_node-main == Q_node-75c43b0` is a direct, bitwise-verified fact for this oracle (not just a same-range inference), which in turn means `main` really does currently resolve to this exact commit. This verifies TODAY's state only, not a permanent guarantee; recommend the production server-side encoder (whenever built) explicitly pin this revision rather than track `main`, so a future upstream repo change can't silently drift the server out from under the frozen corpus vectors.
encoder_execution.note: Correction from the original Phase A version: q8 vs fp32 is NOT a different embedding_space -- it's a different numerical realization of the SAME model, i.e. v_q8(x) ~= v_fp32(x), not two incommensurable spaces. A server-side fp32 encoder stays validly comparable against dsrs-v1 corpus vectors; it just isn't bit-for-bit reproducible. Recommend the server default to q8 anyway to minimize drift rather than rely on Phase C's golden-vector test to catch it after the fact -- but 'meaningless' (this profile's original wording) overstated the risk.

measured_drift_2026-08-15.method: Phase C0/C1: 30-query golden set, real browser-q8 vectors captured from the live production encoder (registry/embedding-profiles/oracle/), compared against a Node.js reference encoder using the SAME library/model/dtype (only the JS runtime differs) -- scripts/phase-c-encoder-compare/. This is the first actual measurement; earlier profile versions correctly flagged it as unmeasured rather than assuming a number.
measured_drift_2026-08-15.cos_browser_q8_vs_node_q8: min 0.996808, max 1.000000 across 30 queries -- same library+model+dtype, different runtime only, effectively identical.
measured_drift_2026-08-15.cos_browser_q8_vs_node_fp32: min 0.982798, max 0.988165 across 30 queries -- real, consistent, small (~1.2-1.7% cosine distance) drift from dtype alone.
measured_drift_2026-08-15.retrieval_drift_document_namespace: 30/30 queries: identical top-1 result between browser-q8 and node-q8 query vectors (mean top-10 overlap 9.97/10). Confirmed BOTH via live Vectorize (default approximate scoring) AND via Phase C1.2's exact local cosine sweep (zero ANN involvement) -- same 30/30 result both ways.
measured_drift_2026-08-15.retrieval_drift_chunk_namespace: 29/30 under EACH method, but NOT the same query -- two independent, separately-caused near-tie flips, not one issue confirmed twice. (1) Via live Vectorize (approximate scoring): mismatch on 'best pizza recipe' (an off-topic control query; ANN approximation noise on weakly-relevant near-tied candidates). (2) Via Phase C1.2's exact cosine sweep (zero ANN, isolates pure encoder drift): mismatch on '機器如何理解語言背後的意圖' (a zero-lexical-overlap paraphrase test) -- browser top-3 = [lm-001669#chunk-1 0.5728, lm-001669#chunk-0 0.5701, lm-001672#chunk-2 0.5701], node-q8 top-3 = [lm-001672#chunk-2 0.5785, lm-001669#chunk-1 0.5784, lm-001669#chunk-0 0.5766] -- both encoders agree on the SAME two source documents, only the #1/#2 slot swaps under a ~0.00003 score gap, a genuine but harmless sub-thousandth-cosine encoder-drift effect on an already near-tied ranking, not a retrieval-quality regression.
measured_drift_2026-08-15.conclusion: Confirms the note above empirically: a server-side q8 encoder (same library/model) reproduces browser retrieval with negligible drift, and this holds even under exact (non-approximate) scoring, isolating encoder drift from Vectorize's ANN approximation as a separate, independently-confirmed-small source of noise. fp32 drift is measurably real but still very small at the vector level; its retrieval-level impact was not separately tested (only q8-vs-q8 was pushed through comparisons) -- if a production server ever runs fp32, retrieval-drift should be re-measured, not assumed to extrapolate linearly from the vector-level number.

index_profile.document_projection: title + summary + headings, newline-joined, empty parts dropped -- see scripts/build_embeddings.py _embed_text(). A document with none of these (no embeddable text) is excluded from this count entirely, not given a zero vector -- see zero_vector_policy below.
index_profile.chunker: "Phase 5" section-based chunker, spec at content/papers/2026/2026-07/02_動態語義顯影_本地端實作技術白皮書_v0.1.md (lm-001862) §17.2/§17.3. No separate machine-readable chunker_version field exists yet in chunk-embeddings-manifest.json; this profile is the first place that version is named explicitly.
index_profile.stable_id_scheme: document: lm-XXXXXX (registry paper id). chunk: {doc_id}#chunk-{index}, e.g. "lm-000001#chunk-0" -- confirmed as the literal key format in registry/generated/chunk-embeddings-manifest.json's `chunks` map (0-based, unpadded). Note: the architecture decision doc's §9 illustrative example used zero-padded chunk ids ("lm-001862#chunk-004") -- that was illustrative, not a spec; the real data is unpadded and Phase B should migrate the real scheme, not the example's padding.
index_profile.zero_vector_policy: Two distinct behaviors, do not conflate them. (1) Build-time / persisted storage (registry/generated/embeddings.f32.bin + embeddings-manifest.json, the Phase B migration source): documents with no embeddable text are skipped entirely -- never written, never counted. This is why document_vectors=2675 while the corpus has 2676 total papers. (2) Build-time / dist output only (dist/ai/semantic-vectors.bin, NOT a migration source): the one missing document is padded with an explicit all-zero vector purely so the frontend's index-aligned array stays in lockstep with semantic-index.min.json's documents array -- an alignment convenience for the browser, not part of the corpus's real vector data. (3) Query-time (both browser and any future server retriever must replicate this): a zero-norm or sub-floor result is excluded from the candidate map outright (`if (norm > 0) scores.set(...)`), never scored 0 and kept. Phase B's exporter must read (1), never (2) -- confirmed empirically: 0 zero-norm vectors found in registry/generated/embeddings.f32.bin across all 2675 entries.
index_profile.doc_chunk_aggregation: max(doc-level score, best chunk-level score) per document, post floor/ceiling rescale -- see shell/public/semantic/semantic-vector.js: `if (norm > 0 && (!existing || norm > existing.score))`. The winning source is tagged ("doc" | "chunk") and, for chunk wins, carries the matched section's heading for hit-reason display -- this per-document folding is an index_profile-level policy choice (how multiple vectors resolve to one relevance signal per document), independent of both the embedding_space and the fusion_profile that later combines this semantic channel with lexical/exact/etc. Phase B's Vectorize implementation (scripts/export_vectorize.py) preserves this same doc/chunk-are-separate-pools structure natively via Vectorize `namespace` (document vs chunk) -- namespace filtering applies before the ANN search, not as a post-filter, so a query still gets independent top-K candidates from each pool before any max-folding, rather than one flat 2675+15616 pool where chunks (5.8x more numerous) would dominate.
index_profile.note: Introduced 2026-08-15 in response to the web-side AI collaborator's second review round. Does not change any Phase A.1 verdict -- embedding_space=dsrs-v1 is unaffected by chunking policy. A future re-chunking (different span size, different heading-boundary rule, different aggregation) gets a new index_profile id (e.g. dsrs-index-v2) and can be A/B'd against dsrs-index-v1 while embedding_space stays fixed at dsrs-v1, exactly like encoder_execution/score_calibration/fusion_profile already do.

score_calibration.formula: score = 0 if raw<=floor; 1 if raw>=ceiling; else (raw-floor)/(ceiling-floor)
score_calibration.sub_floor_behavior: results with raw<=floor are excluded from the semantic candidate map entirely (not merely assigned score 0 and left in) -- see semantic-vector.js: `if (norm > 0) scores.set(...)`
score_calibration.calibrated_against: 1881-document corpus sample, spread of queries from clearly-unrelated (~0.47-0.48 best-match ceiling) to deeply-covered topic (~0.68 for genuinely on-topic Riemann Hypothesis hits)
score_calibration.caveat: Calibrated when the corpus had ~1881 documents. As of 2026-08-15 the corpus has 2676 total papers, of which 2675 have embeddable text and a real vector (one paper has no title/summary/headings text to embed and gets build_embeddings.py's documented all-zero vector -- an intentional edge case, not data loss). The floor/ceiling has not been re-validated at this larger scale. Earlier drafts of this profile inconsistently wrote '2675' in one place and '2676' in another; 2675 is the correct count of EMBEDDED documents, 2676 is the correct count of TOTAL corpus papers -- both numbers are real, they just measure different things.
score_calibration.domain_requirement_for_vectorize_2026-08: This floor/ceiling was fit against EXACT/raw cosine (the browser computes full-precision dot products against in-memory float32 vectors, no approximation anywhere). Vectorize's DEFAULT query scoring is documented as approximate (`developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/best-practices/query-vectors/`: 'returned scores will be an approximation of the real distance/similarity'); high-precision (near-exact) scoring requires `returnValues: true` on the query. Feeding Vectorize's default approximate score into this calibration function applies it outside the domain it was fit on -- most consequentially right at the floor (0.50), where the measured approximate-vs-exact gap this session (~0.877 vs 1.0 on a self-match) is far larger than the floor's own margin, so a candidate could flip between 'excluded entirely' and 'included' depending on scoring mode alone, not real relevance. Any server-side implementation reproducing THIS calibration (dsrs-v1 + corpus-1881-v1) must query Vectorize with `returnValues: true`; using default scoring against this same floor/ceiling would be silently evaluating a different, unvalidated score domain. (Note: topK is capped at 50 when returnValues:true or returnMetadata:'all' is set -- confirmed sufficient for this profile's use, well above any planned top-N.)

fusion_profile.method: per-channel max fusion -- NOT Reciprocal Rank Fusion
fusion_profile.mechanism: scoreCorpus() (shell/public/semantic/semantic-core.js) scores each channel (exact/lexical/alias/related_term/semantic/relation) independently per document; the semantic channel contributes weights.semantic(0.55) * calibrated_score; the document's final score is the MAX across every channel that fired (`if (s > r.score) r.score = s`), never a sum or a rank-based combination.
fusion_profile.note: Correction from the original Phase A handoff: that document said feeding raw cosine into RRF would rank differently than the browser. That framing assumed the browser does something RRF-like; it verifiably does not (confirmed directly against semantic-core.js). Within (floor, ceiling) the linear rescale is strictly monotonic, so under a genuinely rank-based fusion it would not by itself change semantic-channel rank order. What actually matters for comparing fusion policies: (1) sub-floor candidates are excluded outright, (2) super-ceiling candidates tie at 1.0, and (3) most importantly, max-fusion (score-based, what the browser does today) and RRF (rank-based, what the architecture doc proposes for the MCP) are different algorithms that can produce different final orderings even given identical per-channel inputs. RRF is a deliberate NEW fusion_profile for the MCP, not a reproduction of browser-maxfusion-v1 -- that should be stated as a conscious design choice, not implied to be behavior-preserving.

vectorize_deployments.created_via: scripts/export_vectorize.py output, uploaded with `wrangler vectorize create` + `wrangler vectorize upsert` x 5 shards (docs-000, chunks-000..003)
vectorize_deployments.smoke_test: queried both namespaces by an existing vector's own --vector-id, default (approximate) scoring: document namespace top-1 = the queried id itself (self-match score 0.877, next two topically coherent); chunk namespace top-1 = the queried id itself (self-match score 0.858, next two were other chunks of the SAME source document). Self-match well below 1.0 under default scoring is expected under Cloudflare's documented default approximate-scoring path -- not evidence of export/upload precision loss; do not attribute it to a specific mechanism (e.g. 'quantization', or any specific accuracy percentage) Cloudflare's current official docs do not state.
vectorize_deployments.precision_smoke_test_2026-08-15: same two queries rerun with --return-values (Cloudflare's documented high-precision scoring path). Both self-matches scored EXACTLY 1 (document: lm-000502=1, then lm-000775=0.830, lm-001507=0.742; chunk: lm-000216#chunk-4=1, then #chunk-2=0.891, #chunk-5=0.888 -- note high-precision reordered/resharpened the runners-up vs. the approximate pass, consistent with Cloudflare's claim that returnValues:true 'increases the precision of the query matches scores as well as the accuracy of the query results'). This is the direct, measured confirmation that the earlier <1.0 self-match scores were purely a default-scoring-mode artifact, not upload data loss -- superseding the unmeasured 'internal quantization' guess in smoke_test above.
vectorize_deployments.note: First real Vectorize resource for this corpus. Name deliberately encodes embedding_space+index_profile (E+I), not the full E+Q+I+C+F -- see index_profile.note and migration_note. A future index_profile bump gets its own index name, e.g. logic-matrix-dsrs-v1-index-v2, rather than overwriting this one.

migration_note: Any future embedding_space (dsrs-v1.1, dsrs-v2, ...) that changes model, tokenizer, dimension, normalization, query instruction, or document instruction must get its own id and its own file in this directory -- never overwrite this one. Chunking policy is NOT an embedding_space trigger (corrected 2026-08-15 -- it was wrongly listed here in Phase A.1): a change to chunk span size, heading-boundary rule, document-projection text, or doc/chunk aggregation gets a new index_profile id instead (e.g. dsrs-index-v2), while embedding_space stays dsrs-v1. encoder_execution / index_profile / score_calibration / fusion_profile may each version independently of embedding_space and of each other (e.g. embedding_space=dsrs-v1 + encoder_execution=server-q8-v1 + index_profile=dsrs-index-v1 + score_calibration=corpus-2675-v2 + fusion_profile=mcp-rrf-v1 is a valid, expected combination for the MCP -- same coordinate space, deliberately different execution/indexing/calibration/fusion choices). See architecture decision doc §7, §19-21 (DSRS-v2 must be a shadow index, benchmarked, never silently promoted).
